title: Data analyst says APS is shifting data center energy costs to others. AG calls for investigation
key_facts: Arizona Attorney General Kris Mayes urged the Arizona Corporation Commission, in an Oct. 9 letter, to investigate claims that Arizona Public Service (APS) shifted millions of dollars in costs of serving large industrial customers onto others.
Data analyst Abhay Padgaonkar says about 100 data centers and other large industrial users drove nearly all the increase in demand on APS's system in recent years.
His analysis, sent to the commission on Oct. 2, says large users may have underpaid by 600 million dollars for their energy as others picked up the tab.
APS responded on X that it is ensuring residential and small-business customers are not paying for data-center power usage.

A commission spokesperson said the commission disagrees with the analysis, that Padgaonkar did not intervene in the current rate case, and that APS's spending is being audited by staff and 23 other intervenors.
Mayes asked APS to show, using its records, why the analysis is incorrect.
quote_evidence: An analysis he sent to the commission on Oct. 2 shows large users may have underpaid by $600 million for their energy over that period, as others picked up the tab.
The simple fact is: APS is ensuring that residential and small-business customers are not paying for data center power usage.
Late in the day on Oct. 9, a commission spokesperson emailed news desks across the state with a statement that the commission disagrees with Padgaonkar’s analysis.
why_it_matters_hint: Arizona's top legal officer wants regulators to test a claim that data centers are being subsidised by other customers.
notes: Follows 12News reporting (our 5 Oct edition, item 51: APS customers paid about 587 million dollars toward data-center growth, APS denies); KJZZ itself links Padgaonkar's analysis to 12News's reporting but does not say the figures are identical.
